articles.title: La broma del Pedro Sánchez más "jugón" a costa de los Knicks de la NBA y el Mundial de España
articles.summary: Pedro Sánchez, presidente del Gobierno de España y secretario general del PSOE, se acuerda del triunfo de Knicks en la NBA y de España en el Mundial en un discurso en Nueva York ante el mediático alcalde Zohran Mamdani.
articles.body: Pedro Sánchez, presidente del Gobierno de España y secretario general del PSOE, se acuerda del triunfo de Knicks en la NBA y de España en el Mundial en un discurso en Nueva York ante el mediático alcalde Zohran Mamdani. "Los Knicks ganaron el campeonato de la NBA. Y España ganó el Mundial. Así que quizás, alcalde, sólo queda una cosa por demostrar: que las políticas progresistas también pueden ganar el futuro", dijo Pedro Sánchez en el acto denominado Construir una economía para la mayoría. Desde la cuenta oficial del PSOE en Instagram destacaron que "hoy Pedro Sánchez está jugón".

articles.title: La española Awa Fam cierra su primera temporada en la WNBA con récord de puntos
articles.standfirst: Awa FAm anotó 22 puntos, la cifra más alta de su carrera, en el último partido de su temporada de novata
articles.summary: Awa FAm anotó 22 puntos, la cifra más alta de su carrera, en el último partido de su temporada de novata
articles.body: Awa Fam cerró su primera temporada en la WNBA, en la que ha promediado 10,3 puntos y 5,9 rebotes por partido tras haber sido elegida en el número tres del 'draft' por las Seattle Storm. La española tuvo un adiós agridulce a su primera temporada, con un récord de puntos -22- en una nueva derrota de Seattle por 91-103 frente a las Dallas Wings. Fam firmó 22 puntos, 7 rebotes y un tapón en este, el último partido de la temporada de las Storm, que no disputarán los 'playoff'. Fam llegó a la WNBA con la temporada empezada, después de acordar con las Storm terminar la campaña con el Valencia Basket. Unas semanas antes, había hecho historia al convertirse en la española seleccionada más arriba en un 'draft' de la WNBA. La valenciana ha disputado 37 partidos, 26 como titular, para una media de 10,3 puntos, 5,9 rebotes, 1,8 asistencias, 0,8 robos y 0,8 tapones por encuentro en su temporada de 'rookie'. Fam cierra la temporada con 380 puntos y 220 rebotes. Con 20 años, la de Santa Pola se ha convertido en la jugadora más joven de la historia de la WNBA en alcanzar los 50 triples y los 200 rebotes, en una liga en la que la mayoría de jugadoras llegan después su paso por la universidad. Sin embargo, la temporada de las Storm ha dejado mucho que desear. En plena reconstrucción, Seattle termina la campaña como el último equipo de la liga, con un balance de 8-36, por debajo incluso de las dos franquicias debutantes: Toronto Tempo y Portland Fire.

articles.title: El Real Madrid inicia la reconquista
articles.standfirst: Los blancos, campeones en 2023 y finalistas en cuatro de las últimas cinco ediciones, abren en Dubái una Euroliga en la que quieren volver a reinar con Pedro Martínez
articles.summary: Los blancos, campeones en 2023 y finalistas en cuatro de las últimas cinco ediciones, abren en Dubái una Euroliga en la que quieren volver a reinar con Pedro Martínez
articles.body: El Real Madrid estrena su Euroliga en el Coca-Cola Arena de Dubái (18.00 horas) con un objetivo que va mucho más allá de este primer partido: volver a levantar el trofeo. El equipo blanco ha sido finalista en 2022, campeón en 2023, finalista otra vez en 2024 y, más recientemente, en 2026. Con una plantilla reforzada y renovadas ambiciones, el Madrid quiere recuperar el trono europeo. Ya le toca volver a reinar. El primer capítulo de esa reconquista es ante el mismo rival al que derrotó hace seis días en las semis de la novedosa SuperCup de la Euroliga. El Dubai Basketball puso contra las cuerdas al Madrid, que remontó 16 puntos y acabó ganando 95-98 en la prórroga. "Deberíamos ser capaces de estar ya preparados desde el minuto uno. Luego estar agresivos en defensa y la lucha por el rebote va a ser muy importante. Ellos son bastante físicos y el rebote es donde más se puede ver", analiza Pedro Martínez, que se estrena en la Euroliga como entrenador madridista. Ahora el escenario cambia y también la exigencia: comienza la Euroliga y cada partido cuenta en el camino hacia Abu Dabi, sede de la próxima Final Four. "Empezamos de cero, sin pensar demasiado en lo anterior. Sabemos que es una competición tremendamente difícil para todo el mundo. Son 38 partidos y todos los equipos tienen momentos buenos y momentos malos a lo largo del año. Se vio la temporada pasada que con tantísimos partidos es muy difícil mantener un nivel muy alto para todos y hay que estar mentalmente muy preparado", explica Pedro Martínez. El Madrid ha aprovechado estos días en los emiratos, donde se quedó tras ganar la SuperCup, para trabajar sin viajes de por medio y llega con todos sus efectivos salvo Usman Garuba, lesionado de larga duración, y Nick Smith Jr., que viajó pero aún no ha sido dado de alta en la máxima competición continental. Dubai, reforzado con Shengelia, Okobo, Mintz, Blossomgame, Diakite y el recién llegado Walkup, será la primera prueba de verdad. Xavi Pascual ha construido un equipo para competir con los grandes, cosa que intentará este jueves pese a la baja del exmadridista Dzanan Musa, y la duda de Prepelic, otro ex. Sí estará Petrusev.

articles.title: Gregg Popovich se casa con 77 años con la ex de su entrenador asistente durante 17 temporadas
articles.standfirst: Gregg Popovich y Mike Budenholzer ganaron juntos cuatro anillos de la NBA con los San Antonio Spurs
articles.summary: Gregg Popovich y Mike Budenholzer ganaron juntos cuatro anillos de la NBA con los San Antonio Spurs
articles.body: Gregg Popovich, uno de los mejores entrenadores de la historia de la NBA, se ha casado con 77 años. El mítico técnico de los San Antonio Spurs, tal y como adelanta TMZ (tuvo acceso a la licencia de matrimonio), contrajo matrimonio con Mary Barth Budenholzer, la exmujer de su entrenador asistente Mike Budenholzer. Los recién casados intercambiaron sus anillos de boda el 16 de septiembre en Texas... según la licencia de matrimonio registrada en el condado de Bexar (Texas). Mike Budenholzer trabajó como entrenador asistente a las órdenes de Gregg Popovich en los Spurs durante 17 temporadas —de 1996 a 2013— antes de marcharse para asumir el puesto de entrenador jefe de los Atlanta Hawks. Juntos ganaron campeonatos de la NBA con los San Antonio Spurs Mike y Mary se divorciaron discretamente en 2016 y en 2018 murió Erin Popovich, la primera esposa de Pop.

articles.title: El KO, el juego que pone a prueba a los aficionados: elige un ganador, sobrevive y no podrás repetir equipo
articles.standfirst: El nuevo juego de acb Play obliga a elegir un ganador diferente cada jornada y premia al último superviviente con tres fines de semana de baloncesto
articles.summary: El nuevo juego de acb Play obliga a elegir un ganador diferente cada jornada y premia al último superviviente con tres fines de semana de baloncesto
articles.body: La Liga Endesa estrena un juego en el que cada jornada puede ser la última. El KO llega a acb Play con una mecánica sencilla y exigente: elegir un equipo ganador cada semana y sobrevivir. Si pierde, mueres. Si gana, sigues vivo, aunque ese equipo ya no podrá volver a ser elegido. Una decisión que apenas lleva un minuto puede acompañarte durante toda la semana porque un solo fallo supone la eliminación. Cada participante dispone de una única oportunidad. En cada jornada deberá escoger un equipo que crea que va a ganar su partido. El contador de supervivientes irá bajando semana tras semana hasta el término de la primera vuelta. El reto pasa por superar las 17 jornadas y para conseguirlo habrá que acertar 17 ganadores diferentes sin cometer un solo error. Con 18 equipos disponibles, llegará un momento en el que tocará confiar incluso en ese rival que nunca elegirías en otras circunstancias. El último superviviente optará a un premio único. El ganador podrá elegir tres partidos de la segunda vuelta y vivir tres fines de semana con viaje, hotel y entradas para un partido para dos personas. El plazo para apuntarse termina el sábado 26 de septiembre a las 18:00h, coincidiendo con el comienzo de la Liga Endesa 2026-27. A partir de ahí, cada elección marcará la continuidad en el juego. El mecanismo se sostiene sobre dos normas. La primera obliga a elegir cada jornada un equipo al que el participante vea ganador: si acierta, continúa; si falla, queda eliminado. La segunda añade toda la estrategia. Cada equipo solo puede utilizarse una vez durante las 17 jornadas. Escoger a uno en la primera fecha significa renunciar a él durante el resto del juego, por muy favorable que resulte alguno de sus siguientes partidos. Hay 18 equipos para 17 jornadas, así que prácticamente todos tendrán que entrar en los planes tarde o temprano. El juego incluye además un comodín. Cada usuario podrá utilizarlo una sola vez y tendrá de plazo hasta el final del tercer cuarto del partido elegido. Si el encuentro se tuerce y la apuesta pinta mal, podrá activar ese recurso y salvar la jornada. Una vez gastado, desaparece cualquier margen de seguridad para lo que quede de primera vuelta. Una estrategia para sobrevivir 17 jornadas El KO obliga a mirar el partido inmediato y, al mismo tiempo, todo el calendario. No basta con localizar al favorito de cada jornada. También hay que decidir cuándo gastar cada equipo, medir qué opciones pueden aparecer más adelante y administrar un comodín que solo ofrece una vida extra. Guardar demasiado a un conjunto puede dejarlo sin utilidad; utilizarlo demasiado pronto puede echarse de menos semanas después. Un solo fallo, en cualquier jornada, termina la partida. No hay una segunda oportunidad más allá de ese comodín ni posibilidad de recuperar un equipo ya utilizado. Durante 17 jornadas, el participante tendrá que combinar conocimiento de la Liga Endesa, estrategia y sangre fría mientras el contador de supervivientes se reduce semana tras semana.

articles.title: Legendary Lakers PA announcer Lawrence Tanter dies at 76
articles.summary: Longtime Lakers public address announcer Lawrence Tanter has died at age 76, the team announced.
articles.body: Longtime Lakers public address announcer Lawrence Tanter has died at age 76, the team announced. Tanter had been the Lakers’ public address announcer through the 2025- 26 season. The team announced in June that Tanter retired from the position but would remain with the organization as its special adviser for game presentation. “We are deeply saddened to share the news of the passing of legendary Lakers public address announcer Lawrence Tanter,’’ the team announced Wednesday night. “For 43 years, LT’s voice served as the soundtrack to Lakers games at the arena. He will be remembered as a cherished member of the Lakers family.’’ Tanter’s tenure with the Lakers spanned 10 NBA championships, 16 Western Conference titles and some of the most successful eras in franchise history. During the NBA’s pandemic-era bubble in 2020, Tanter recorded game introductions from his home studio to help recreate the familiar atmosphere of Lakers basketball. Tanter was also a disc jockey for Los Angeles-area radio stations KJLH, KTWV and KKJZ.

articles.title: LeBron James’ longtime business partner Maverick Carter clashes with ex Crystal Streets over daughter's child support
articles.summary: LeBron James’ longtime business partner and childhood friend Maverick Carter is facing a court battle with his ex-partner Crystal Streets over child
articles.body: LeBron James’ longtime business partner and childhood friend Maverick Carter is facing a court battle with his ex-partner Crystal Streets over child support payments. Court documents show Carter has asked a judge to stop the $25,000 monthly payments he currently makes for their daughter.Carter says their 18-year-old daughter lives at a full-time boarding school, whose costs he pays in full. He argues that Streets has little “meaningful” custodial time because their daughter lives away at school. Streets disagrees and wants the payments to continue until their daughter graduates.Maverick Carter asks court to end $25K monthly child support paymentsAccording to court documents seen by TMZ, MaverickCarter is seeking to reduce his monthly child support obligation from $25,000 to $0. He says the request is not an attempt to avoid supporting his daughter. Instead, he argues that he pays directly for everything she needs.Carter’s legal team also pointed to the fact that their daughter turned 18 in July. He argued that the court no longer had jurisdiction over custody matters involving her after she reached adulthood.The businessman is represented in the case by high-profile family law attorney Laura Wasser.Streets has challenged Carter’s request. She claims Carter is worth more than $100 million and should continue paying support while their daughter finishes school.She has asked the court to increase the monthly payment to $35,000. Streets also claims that she and Carter agreed to the higher amount in 2024. However, she says the agreement was never finalized because of the California wildfires.Streets has also rejected Carter’s description of her role in their daughter’s life. She says she continues to provide emotional support and remains involved in her daughter’s day-to-day needs.According to the court documents, Streets says she also coordinates travel and provides for her daughter even though she is currently living at boarding school.The case also includes alleged emails between Carter and Streets. One email, dated December 28, 2025, appears to have been sent by Carter to his former partner.In the message, he allegedly wrote, “Dealing with you is the only thing bad about my life, and I’ll be soooo happy when it’s over.”The dispute came before a judge at a hearing on September 15. Streets argued that Carter’s child support payments should not be terminated.Carter disagreed and maintained his position that the payments should end.The court has not yet issued a final ruling on the dispute. For now, Carter’s child support obligations have been suspended for three months while the court considers the arguments made by both sides.The legal battle comes as Carter remains widely known for his longtime relationship with LeBron James. The pair have been childhood friends and business partners for years, with Carter playing a major role in James’ business ventures and media projects.The latest court proceedings, however, are focused on Carter’s financial obligations and his dispute with Streets over support for their daughter.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranking the NBA's Best Young Cores Right Now
articles.summary: Young NBA talent is, by its very nature, exciting.
articles.body:
Young NBA talent is, by its very nature, exciting.

What feels perhaps different now more than ever, though, is that there doesn't have to be any delay between that excitement and the realization of what it can become.

While young hoopers often tantalize for what they might become tomorrow, some of them are genuine juggernauts today. You might notice, then, some direct overlap between this conversation of the Association's best young cores and general power rankings of teams as a whole.

There are, of course, still some "They got next" rebuilders who are flooded with youth but impacted by all the uncertainty that so often comes along with it. There just also happens to be some "They got now" powerhouses who can go (and have gone) toe-to-toe with the top-ranked heavyweights in the entire hoops world.

Speaking of rankings, let's dig into the discussion at hand by sorting the league's best young cores—weighing players in their age-24 seasons or younger—by everything from high-end talent and on-paper production to on-court cohesiveness and long-term potential.

The Hornets pack a powerful 1-2 punch with their young core led by 21-year-old Kon Knueppel (silver medalist in last season's Rookie of the Year voting) and 23-year-old Brandon Miller (20.2 points on 43.5/38.3/89.2 shooting in 2025-26). They just don't have many known contributors beyond them. Sion James looks solid but not special, and there are questions about first-round rookies Hannes Steinbach (perimeter utility) and Christian Anderson Jr. (lack of size and strength).

It's tempting to reserve Dallas a top-five spot here by virtue of rostering reigning Rookie of the Year winner Cooper Flagg alone. It just feels hard to justify that when he is sort of on an island with Dereck Lively II struggling to stay on the court, and the NBA odometers showing goose eggs for first-round rookies Morez Johnson Jr. and Sergio de Larrea.

If these rankings went six spots deep, the Grizzlies would've made the cut. And some will argue they still belong in the top five given Cameron Boozer's polish, Cedric Coward's production and Zach Edey's flashes. That said, if Boozer winds up closer to good than great, Memphis might be missing a true needle-mover, with Coward perhaps bumping into his ceiling soon (he's already 23) and Edey facing agility limitations.

It should be obvious pretty early into the season whether the Jazz are ranked too high, too low or just right. Because, honestly, things could go just about any direction from here.

Plenty will depend on the readiness and impact of No. 2 pick Darryn Peterson. He was, in the eyes of many, the best prospect in his class. ESPN's Jeremy Woo put Peterson atop his 2026 draft big board and called him "the most gifted scorer in the draft," "a ramarkable long-range shotmaker" and "a strong athlete with good size for a ball-handler."

If Peterson gets back the explosiveness and playmaking he showcased late in his prep career, he could be a full-fledged, two-way star. He's also far from the only swing factor in Salt Lake City. There are also eyeballs on Keyonte George and the sustainability of his third-year breakout, a possible sophomore leap for scoring swingman Ace Bailey and the developmental hurdles cleared (or plowed into) by Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh and Kyle Filipowski.

A touch more certainty is needed to slot these young Jazz any higher, in other words, but ample potential remains within that unpredictability. A banner year from this bunch could vault it into a top-three ranking and perhaps even help Utah crash the playoff party.

The Rockets may not be first to mind when thinking of a young team, but they aren't lacking for young talent.

Alperen Şengün, who turned 24 in July, is already a two-time All-Star who flourishes as a 6'11" offensive hub. Amen Thompson, who will be 24 in January, is an all-purpose defensive stopper and athletic 6'7" playmaker. Throw in 23-year-old Jabari Smith Jr. (functionally a 6'11" three-and-D forward) and 22-year-old Reed Sheppard (a sharpshooter with some creation chops), and this is a core than shine on either end of the court.

Is it lacking quantity? Maybe, but quality is always the true aim, and Houston has that in spades. Şengün is an established star, and Thompson might be a couple offensive improvements away from superstardom. Smith is, at worst, a rock-solid starter, and Sheppard's best-case scenarios let the imagination run wild .

Houston's win-right-now timeline doesn't leave a ton of wiggle room for growing pains, but these players have all handled the pressure in ways that makes you forget they might all have big developmental jumps still in front of them. That is a scary thought—well, it is anywhere outside of Space City, at least.

This should not be fair. A team this successful—back-to-back seasons with NBA-best win totals, six series triumphs (including the 2025 Finals) in this stretch—should not have this much young talent at its disposal. Having Sam Presti calling the shots, it seems, is no less than a real-life cheat code.

OKC can point toward both star power and strength in numbers as reasons behind its bronze medal here. Chet Holmgren just captured third-team All-NBA and first-team All-Defensive honors. Cason Wallace, who has yet to hold a full-time starting role, just snagged an All-Defensive second-team spot. If Ajay Mitchell's rising star appears cloudy at all, it's only due to the ridiculous depth of this roster.

Speaking of which, that's merely the foundation of this celebrated young core. Because there's been no mention yet of slithery shot-maker Jared McCain, nor of sturdy and stretch-y (and savvy) center Jaylin Williams. Never mind the many first-rounders who have hardly played (Nikola Topić) or have yet to debut (Aday Mara, Bennett Stirtz, Thomas Sorber).

This is, in technical economic terms, an absurd embarassment of riches. And yet, the core is still confined to merely the No. 3 spot due to the wealth of ascending (and, in many ways, established) talent still in front of it.

Some might quibble over Washington's placement, since this core lacks the league-wide accolades of the few right behind it. Where the Wizards can counter, though, is with the documented growth of their group already and the vast untapped potential still ahead of it.

They are overloaded with recent first-round picks to the point that the idea of listing them all carries the worry of not having enough digital ink to cover the lot: AJ Dybantsa (No. 1 in 2026), Tre Johnson (No. 6 in 2025), Will Riley (No. 21 in 2025), Alex Sarr (No. 2 in 2024), Bub Carrington (No. 14 in 2024), Kyshawn George (No. 24 in 2024) and Bilal Coulibaly (No. 7 in 2023). Tristan Vukčević (No. 42 in 2023) isn't offically part of that group, but he might be a first-rounder in a re-draft.

You know what that core all has in common, besides the draft pedigree? They're all under the age of 24. And save for Dybantsa, a possible Tracy McGrady clone , they all have encouraging track records, too. The core kind of has everything: ignitable shooting, slippery shot-creation, electric slashing, defensive versatility, quick-strike scoring.

In fact, is has more (by quantity) than even the No. 1 ranked core on this list. It's just missing a legitimate superstar, which is kind of a big deal when our gold medalists happen to have a 22-year-old pushing for best-player-on-the-planet status and two 21-and-under sidekicks showing star trajectories of their own.

The quartet featured above—all age 22 or under—just all filled regular playoff rotation minutes for a 62-win NBA Finalist. Victor Wembanyama served as the centerpiece, Stephon Castle joined him in the starting five, Dylan Harper arguably deserved a starting spot and Carter Bryant drew one marquee matchup after another .

San Antonio may not have much else for the purpose of this exercise—it's wait-and-see with first-round rookies Jayden Quaintance and Tarris Reed Jr.—but it doesn't need anything else. Such is the luxury of snagging three consecutive top-four picks and turning them into Wembanyama (No. 1 in 2023), Castle (No. 4 in 2024) and Harper (No. 2 in 2025).

Their ages suggest they could be years away from maxing out their potential. Incredibly, the eye test tells a similar tale. Wembanyama, as great as he is, is still finding his go-to scoring strength (as a 51-percent shooting 25-point scorer). Castle's jumper remains a work in progress. Harper could stand to up his distance shooting and playmaking. Carter is ridiculously bounce, but he's also basically a blank slate on offense.

Yet, even while acknowledging all of the improvements still needed, this looks like the foundation of a multi-time championship dynasty. Considering how it has fared so far and how much more it could do with a few developmental successes, that trophy count could start climbing as soon as this season.

articles.title: WNBA gameday discussion: How will playoff seeding shake out for the Golden State Valkyries, Las Vegas Aces, Indiana Fever and Washington Mystics?
articles.summary: On the final day of the WNBA regular season, four playoff seeds remain unsettled.
articles.body:
Following Wednesday's WNBA games, four of eight playoff seeds are now settled.

After the Minnesota Lynx , with an (unwanted?) assist from the Portland Fire , locked down the No. 1 seed on Tuesday, the Atlanta Dream earned the No. 4 seed and homecourt advantage in the first round with a second-straight win over the now-official No. 8-seed New York Liberty . With New York's loss, the Dallas Wings secured the No. 7 seed with their win over the Seattle Storm .

That leaves the No. 2 seed, No. 3 seed, No. 5 seed and No. 6 seed still undetermined. Here's the current state of the standings, with asterisks denoting the seeds that are finalized:

If all of the Golden State Valkyries , Las Vegas Aces, Indiana Fever and Washington Mystics win, things will remain as is. That outcome probably should be the expectation.

However, let's take a closer look at the stakes and scenarios facing the Valkyries, Aces, Fever and Mystics. In the comments, be sure to give your predictions.

Golden State Valkyries vs. Los Angeles Sparks (10 p.m. ET, WNBA League Pass)

The Valkyries are the opponent for the final game of Nneka Ogwumike 's WNBA career.

While a loss would slightly better the Sparks' lottery odds, the team has appeared to prioritize competing with the kind of class Nneka demonstrated throughout her career—they've won their last three games over fellow lottery-bound teams—over any potential percentage bump in lottery balls.

If the Sparks are motivated to send off Nneka with a win, the Valkyries might have a more challenging game than anticipated. They enter with a clean injury report, and plenty of incentive to clinch the No. 2 seed.

With a win, they would set up a first round series against the No. 7-seed Wings. Golden State swept the season series against Dallas, winning the three games by 11 points, 18 points and eight points.

That said, will the Valkyries view avoiding injury as even more valuable?

On Wednesday, the Liberty opted to rest Breanna Stewart , with head coach Chris DeMarco suggesting the decision was "just precautionary with some soreness." (Or, New York wanted the first round series against Minnesota, rather than Golden State or Vegas?)

Unfortunately for the Liberty, their precaution with Stewie was proven particularly smart when Jonquel Jones suffered an ankle injury after stepping on a fan's foot. She was ruled out for the remainder of the game. Early indications are that it is not serious enough to sideline her for the playoffs, with DeMarco sharing that she was "in good spirits" after the game.

Atlanta also experienced an injury scare when Sabrina Ionescu 's errant arm bar hit Angel Reese in the face, sending her back to the locker room and requiring her to miss the start of the second half; Angel eventually returned to the game.

Those plays, however, might be on the mind of Golden State head coach Natalie Nakase as she manages her team's final game.

Las Vegas Aces vs. Phoenix Mercury (10 p.m. ET, USA Network/CNBC)

The WNBA schedule makers thought they were cooking by scheduling a rematch of the 2025 WNBA Finals as the final game for the Aces and Phoenix Mercury.

Of course, when the Mercury saw the Aces across the way on opening day, they delivered what turned out to be their very best performance of the season, blowing out the defending champs on their homecourt. Might Phoenix bookend their season with a similar showing? (Such a circumstance, however, might be more torturous than thrilling for Mercury fans who have had to witness a lot of disappointment between the opener and finale.)

If the Valkyries win, the Aces are stuck in the No. 3 seed, regardless of what happens.

So, I would expect head coach Becky Hammon's hoodied assistants to be closely monitoring the score in LA. If the Valkyries establish a lead, there's no reason to put any extra miles on the Big 3 of A'ja Wilson, Chelsea Gray and Jackie Young . Conversely, if the Sparks are giving it their all for Nneka, the Aces might be motivated to push for the win.

As I noted yesterday , Dallas, the No. 7 seed, had an edge over Vegas this season, possibly incentivizing the Aces to avoid the No. 2 seed.

A decision also could be influenced by which team ends up in the No. 6 seed, as the results of Fever-Lynx should be settled by tip off in Phoenix, if not soon after. Vegas lost the season series to Indiana 1-2, with that one win requiring a near miracle, and won the season over Washington 2-1, although both wins were hard-fought.

Considering the Fever gave the Aces their toughest series during last season's title run, I could see them gunning for the No. 2 seed if Indiana falls to No. 6. But again, that's only possible if it appears Golden State is going to lose to Los Angeles .

Indiana Fever vs. Minnesota Lynx (8 p.m. ET, USA Network)

Even with the No. 1 seed locked up, Olivia Miles is the only rotational regular on the Lynx listed on the injury report.

That means the four starters that head coach Cheryl Reeve benched for the second half of Tuesday's loss in Indiana— Napheesa Collier , Kayla McBride , Courtney Williams and Natasha Howard —will at least start this game, barring a late change to the injury report.

While the motivation behind Reeve's move on Tuesday can be debated as truly about rest, a statement about the starters' play or a possibly failed attempt at playoff matchup manipulation, it would be surprising if any of those four play significant minutes.

The Lynx's absence of incentives should make this a relatively easy Fever win, which would keep them in the No. 5 seed and set up a first-round rematch with the No. 4-seed Dream.

However, Minnesota's deeper reserves, likely aware that they're going to see little, if any, playing time in the playoffs, could cause Indy some troubles. For such players, this is a perfect proving ground for their next contract, whether for an overseas team or next season in the W. They're going to try their best to make Indiana earn that No. 5 seed.

And, are we sure the Fever want the No. 5 seed?

I think so. As mentioned above, they've given the likely No. 3-seed Aces some problems, but angling to play the defending champs over a Dream group that's never won a playoff series together would be insane.

Chicago Sky vs. Washington Mystics (7:30 p.m. ET, WNBA League Pass)

The Chicago Sky's injury report features five names, with more possibly added before tip off.

Washington can add insult to those injuries: Giving the Sky one more L would provide a final lottery-ball boost for the Mystics, as Washington owns Chicago's 2027 first-round pick.

However, I would expect injury avoidance to be DC's top priority, as they are dependent on a Fever loss to escape the No. 6 seed.

Whether they end up as the No. 5 seed or No. 6 seed, the Mystics should enter the playoffs pressure-free as ahead-of-schedule overachievers, which should make the Dream, Aces or Valkyries wary if they end up with Washington on the other side.

articles.title: Olivia Miles is our Rookie of the Year. But who else stood out in a deep WNBA class?
articles.summary: As the playoff picture is finally coming into focus, it’s fitting that the final seeds won’t be settled until the last day of the season. You know what’s not...
articles.body:
As the playoff picture is finally coming into focus, it's fitting that the final seeds won't be settled until the last day of the season.

You know what's not being left until the last day of the season? The Athletic 's experts taking stock of the league and making decisions on year-end awards.

We unveiled our choices for Most Improved Player and Coach of the Year on Wednesday. Now, we continue with our Rookie of the Year and Defensive Player of the Year Award, and Friday, we'll showcase our MVP and All-WNBA teams.

Our experts Annie Costabile, Brian Hamilton, Chantel Jennings and Sabreena Merchant explain their votes.

Olivia Miles was the unanimous pick, and that's no surprise. With her outstanding play, the No. 2 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft played her way into the MVP debate and ran away with the ROY award.

The more contested selections were those who followed Miles. Azzi Fudd, the No. 1 pick in this year's draft, averaged 13 points a game and started 24 of 30 games for the Dallas Wings , earning her the second-place nod, and a three-way tie for third rounds out an exclusively guard-occupied top group of rookies.

Here is the list of rookies who finished in the top 20 for win shares this season: Miles. Here are some players who had fewer win shares than Miles: Allisha Gray , Caitlin Clark , Alyssa Thomas , Angel Reese . It's bonkers, the debut season Miles had. The calls past that were difficult, though, considering Taylor's surprise breakout with the Chicago Sky and Kiki Rice starting and finishing strong, around an injury-related slump in the middle. Fudd didn't finish the season, but she was an emerging two-way standout for Dallas. — Brian Hamilton

Miles is my MVP; that's how good of a rookie she has been. Fudd was a quality starter on a winning team while she was healthy, leading the Wings in on-off differential. Taylor was buried on the bench for too long, but when she was in the starting lineup, she averaged 15.4 points on 35.3 percent shooting from beyond the arc; more importantly, the struggling Sky had a positive point differential in those minutes. A hat tip to Astier, Rice, Lauren Betts and the Seattle Storm duo of Flau'jae Johnson and Awa Fam, all of whom had seasons worthy of the all-rookie team, but it's a deep class. — Sabreena Merchant

The Rookie of the Year race was not close. Miles became the front-runner before the All-Star break when she carried the Minnesota Lynx to the top of the leaderboard without 2025 MVP runner-up Napheesa Collier . The rookie class this year was more about depth than anything. Between Fudd finding her rhythm in Dallas, Taylor being one of the few bright lights in Chicago, and Astier, Rice and Johnson all showing up as significant contributors for their teams, the 2026 rookie class is in the conversation as one of the deepest. — Annie Costabile

In the WNBA's history, only five players have averaged 19-plus points and six-plus assists over the course of a season: Diana Taurasi, Candace Parker, Caitlin Clark (twice), Jackie Young … and Olivia Miles. Among them, Miles averaged the fewest minutes. With all due respect to the other rookies in this class, only one player was completely un-rookie-like and instead played like someone who's putting herself in the same category as the DTs and CPs of the world. — Chantel Jennings

Angel Reese was the only player among our top three who appeared on each of our ballots, earning the top nod from three of our voters. But it was a tightly contested race beyond the top spot, as several players' defensive contributions were recognized.

Unlike the ROY, the DPOY battle spanned positions, which — rightfully so — indicates the deep defensive versatility in the WNBA, a near-necessity now for players, whether they initially get in their stance in the paint or on the perimeter.

Also receiving votes: Sonia Citron , Washington Mystics; Veronica Burton, Golden State Valkyries.

As someone who was never mistaken for an adequate defender on a basketball court, I'm a little hesitant to make appraisals here. So I'll just rely on numbers. Reese finished first in total rebounds, third in defensive rebounds, third in steals, first in defensive win shares and fourth in defensive rating. She can guard all five spots on the floor. Reese is a massive asset for one of the league's top defensive outfits. — Hamilton

Entering the final stretch of regular-season games, Reese was the league leader in defensive win shares, third in defensive rebound percentage, tied for third in defensive boards and tied for first in steal percentage (among players averaging at least five rebounds per game). Among high-usage players, no one has had a better on-off differential for defensive team rating. On top of that, what the stats don't show is her versatility to guard all five positions and her activity that causes deflections, misdirections and turnovers. — Jennings

Williams has been the best defender on the WNBA's top-rated defensive team, but Reese's numbers don't lie. Her stats are impressive, and her defensive prowess is best measured by her overall impact. The Atlanta Dream have the fourth-best defensive rating (103.9) in the league, but it improves to 99.3 when Reese is on the court. — Costabile

Citron is consistently tasked with defending the opponent's best player, and she does it better than any other perimeter defender in the league. Among players who have contested at least 100 shots by All-Stars, Citron allows the lowest effective field goal percentage and the lowest expected shot quality. Put plainly, she forces the best players into the worst possible shots. In a league that emphasizes freedom of movement and is becoming increasingly friendly toward offense from the perimeter, the job of a wing stopper has never been more difficult. Citron still gets it done. — Merchant
authors: Annie Costabile, Brian Hamilton and more

articles.title: Lawrence Tanter, Legendary Lakers PA Announcer, Dies at Age 76
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers announced Thursday that longtime public-address announcer Lawrence Tanter died at the age of 76.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers announced Thursday that longtime public-address announcer Lawrence Tanter died at the age of 76.

Tanter had spent 43 years as the Lakers' PA announcer, dating back to the 1980s, which was a decade that saw L.A. win five championships.

According to ESPN's Dave McMenamin , Tanter retired in June after suffering a stroke and missing the Lakers' final six regular-season home games and the playoffs late in the 2025-26 campaign.

Just before he entered hospice care last month, Tanter texted McMenamin, "Quote me. It's been a blessing."

Originally from Chicago, Tanter spent many years as a DJ on jazz radio stations in addition to his role with the Lakers, per McMenamin.

Over the course of his long and successful career, Tanter was with the Lakers organization for 10 of their 18 championships, including the most recent one in 2020.
